scientific_status: reviewed synthesis will qualify unsupported assertions

review.summary: An audit of the mechanotransduction and organism-resilience literature and codebase indicates that individual lifespan prediction via matrix-YAP loop recovery dynamics (H5) lacks empirical literature support and suffers from model implementation artifacts. While Pyrkov et al. (2021) established systemic resilience recovery clocks in blood/activity data, transferring this concept to local ECM-YAP dynamics is an untested hypothesis. Furthermore, code audit reveals that simulated recovery rates are functionally constrained by the fixed transcriptional parameter tau_M rather than dynamic matrix slowing down.

findings.title: Lit Evidentiary Gap for Mechanotransduction Individual Lifespan Prediction
findings.evidence: Pyrkov et al. (2021) evaluates systemic blood and activity fluctuations, but does not measure ECM-YAP-myosin recovery kinetics or establish individual remaining-lifespan prediction from mechanotransduction dynamics.
findings.implication: Extrapolating systemic physiological resilience clocks to single-cell or tissue mechanotransduction recovery dynamics remains an unvalidated hypothesis.
findings.recommended_check: Conduct longitudinal tracking of single-organism mechanotransduction reporter dynamics alongside lifespan measurement to test predictive power beyond chronological age.

findings.title: Model Recovery Rate Invariance Driven by Fixed Parameter tau_M
findings.evidence: The Jacobian matrix J uses -1/tau_M (-0.167/h) on the diagonal, and empirical dY/dM values in results/cpu32/cell.csv are near zero (ranging -0.004 to 0.005), making the calculated eigenvalue invariant to matrix stiffness changes.
findings.implication: The simulated 'recovery rate slowing' is an artifact of fixed parameterization rather than emergent physical critical slowing down of matrix mechanosensing.
findings.recommended_check: Inspect matrix sensitivity derivatives across a wider range of non-saturated contractilities and report analytical eigenvalue dependencies on tau_Y, tau_M, and dY/dM.

findings.title: Absence of Direct Literature Linking YAP Recovery Kinetics to Lifespan
findings.evidence: Literature searches in swarm round 2 identified upstream regulatory components (YAP export, AMPK, cofilin) but no empirical evidence connecting mechanotransduction recovery kinetics to individual organismal lifespan.
findings.implication: H5 rests entirely on theoretical analogy rather than established biological mechanisms.
findings.recommended_check: Validate whether mechanical perturbation recovery in vivo (e.g. pressure pulse recovery in C. elegans) exhibits age-dependent slowing before claiming clock utility.

review.strongest_surviving_claim: Mechanosensing loops and strain-stiffening ECM networks exhibit age-related changes in baseline stiffness and YAP nuclear localization, but recovery kinetics do not currently support individual lifespan prediction.
review.decisive_next_experiment: Perform age-adjusted longitudinal repeated-measurement pressure-pulse assays on individually housed C. elegans expressing a YAP-1/collagen reporter (WorMotel setup), comparing remaining-lifespan prediction variance explained by recovery rate versus chronological age alone. Falsifier: recovery time provides no statistically significant gain in hazard model log-likelihood over chronological age.

literature_to_verify.query: Pyrkov 2021 dynamic organism level resilience remaining lifespan prediction
literature_to_verify.reason: Verify the empirical boundaries of systemic resilience decay timescales and whether local tissue/matrix dynamics were evaluated.
